input.body:
8 Brindlewick Row, ref NBL-020-01 (R/020). Nora, I'm sorry you've not had safety advice before now. Please treat the warm kitchen socket as unsafe:
1. Don't touch or use the socket, and don't plug anything into it.
2. If you can do it safely with dry hands, open the consumer unit (fuse box) and switch off the breaker marked kitchen/sockets/ring. If you can't tell which one it is, switch off the main switch. Don't take the cover off. The fridge may lose power. That's OK for a few hours, just keep the door shut.
3. If you see smoke, sparks or scorch marks, or the smell gets stronger, take your son outside straight away and call 999.
4. Check your smoke alarm works.
We are arranging an urgent visit from a qualified electrician (Rian Sol, Bracken Spark Services) and our team will phone you shortly to confirm timing. Please tell us if you can't isolate the power.

Dear Mr Vane,

We still haven't been able to reach you about the kitchen socket at 8 Brindlewick Row (ref NBL-020-01). Here is where things stand. The socket has been warm with a burning smell since 08:14 today. Rowan Pike could not get in and does not do fixed-wiring work, so nobody has inspected it. The tenant is at home with her 10-year-old son and the smell is still there.
